raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

**Reproduction** (main `b37e6f79fce`): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next eager PD with Mooncake/MNNVL, prefill `--tp-size 1 --pp-size 4 --disable-overlap-schedule`, decode `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, random ISL/OSL `8192/2`, concurrency 32, and the default four transfer queues. There is no process exception; the raw failure signature is that independent rooms select the same worker while decode accumulates transfer requests:

```
[2026-09-30 23:48:14 PP0] D5_XFER_REQ_BEGIN room=7358507676496413592 worker=3 session=10.49.64.248:15525 last_chunk=True
[2026-09-30 23:48:14 PP1] D5_XFER_REQ_BEGIN room=7358507676496413592 worker=3 session=10.49.64.248:15525 last_chunk=True
[2026-09-30 23:50:29 TP0 EP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, ... #transfer-req: 31, ... gen throughput (token/s): 1.68
```

**Call path:** `MooncakeKVManager.add_transfer_request` hashes the fixed destination-session port sum → every room enters one `transfer_queue` → one `transfer_worker` drains rooms serially → each destination calls `send_kvcache` → `_await_transfer_futures` waits for that room before the worker dequeues the next one. The problem is that the queue key contains no room identity, so a fixed single decode TP replica serializes independent large hybrid KV/state transfers behind one worker.

**Trigger condition:**

- Decode attention TP>1 with one decode instance → the target-session set is fixed → every room lands on only 1/Q queues (the topology reproduced here).
- Decode TP=1 with DEP → each request contributes one random port → expected coverage is `Q·(1−(1−1/Q)^n)=2.73/4` for `n=4,Q=4`, and all four queues are distinct with probability 9.4%, so the old key is mildly imbalanced.
- Multiple decode instances → the router may spread target-session sets across queues, but provides no distribution guarantee.

## Modifications

- Add `_mix_room_id`, a 64-bit SplitMix64 finalizer, in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py`.
- Change `MooncakeKVManager.add_transfer_request` to select `mix(bootstrap_room) % queue_count`; this spreads independent rooms without aliasing DEP room residues, while every chunk of one room still maps to one FIFO.
- Extend `TestMooncakeTransferQueueSharding` with congruent-room distribution, same-room multi-chunk stability, and cross-queue failed-session early-exit coverage. The last case proves that fail-fast uses the manager-wide `failed_sessions` set under `session_lock`, not queue affinity.

2 files changed, +152 / −9.

## Accuracy Tests

Evaluation commands on the PD router:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 50 --num-threads 32 --base-url http://<prefill-node>:<router-port>
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 32 --base-url http://<prefill-node>:<router-port>
```

The error scan covers `Traceback`, `RuntimeError`, `CUDA error`, `OOM`, `NCCL`, `KVTransferError`, `session not alive`, and address/port collisions.

| Model / topology | Revision / job | Examples | Score | Accept length | Transfer errors |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, prefill TP1×PP4 → decode TP4+EP4+NEXTN | main `b37e6f79fce` | 50 | 0.980 | n/a | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, prefill TP1×PP4 → decode TP4+EP4+NEXTN | this PR | 50 | 0.980 | n/a | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, prefill DEP4 → decode TP4+EP4+NEXTN | main `b37e6f79fce` | 50 | 0.980 | n/a | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, prefill DEP4 → decode TP4+EP4+NEXTN | this PR | 50 | 0.980 | n/a | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 8192/1024 C32, d004 | main `b37e6f79fce` / `959180` | 50 | 0.980 | 3.1467 | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 8192/1024 C32, d076 | this PR / `961766` | 50 | 0.960 | 3.1636 | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, eval-only, d004 T05/T06 | main `b37e6f79fce` / `963879` | 200 | 0.965 | 3.1511 | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, eval-only, d004 T05/T06 | this PR / `963879` | 200 | 0.985 | 3.1548 | 0 |

The 50-example 8192/1024 rows are single runs on different pairs and differ by one answer, so they are references rather than a variance estimate. J3 is the accuracy decision: its 200-example before→fixed runs share one allocation and pair, and the exact difference is `4/200=0.020`, which passes the preregistered `|fixed−before|≤0.02` threshold. Both evaluations returned zero and the real-error scans are empty; speculative accept-length means are 3.1511 and 3.1548.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Existing same-allocation C32 / ISL 8192 / OSL 2 results:

| Prefill topology | main tok/s/GPU | this PR tok/s/GPU | Speedup | Per-user TPS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP1×PP4 | 2790.90 | 4830.14 | 1.731× | n/a (OSL=2 diagnostic) |
| DEP4 | 3529.40 | 5363.28 | 1.520× | n/a (OSL=2 diagnostic) |

J1 same-allocation main-Q4 → main-Q1 → fixed-Q4:

| Variant | tok/s/GPU runs | Median | Relative to main Q4 | Busy workers | Critical-room p50 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main Q4 | 2998.05 / 2895.81 / 2903.68 | 2903.68 | 1.000× | 1/4 | 709.911 ms |
| main Q1 | 3661.27 / 3593.96 / 3692.15 | 3661.27 | 1.261× | 1/1 | 554.496 ms |
| this PR Q4 | 5428.68 / 5375.98 / 5108.64 | 5375.98 | 1.851× | 4/4 | 1394.394 ms |

J2 standalone 8192/1024 C32 steady-state points:

| Revision | Job / pair | Active / wall window | Active / wall tok/s/GPU | Per-user TPS mean / P90 | Environment gate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| main `b37e6f79fce` | `959180` / d004 T02/T16 | 3731.806 / 4676 s | 2985.45 / 2382.62 | 51.495 / 50.938 | PASS |
| this PR | `961766` / d076 T15/T16 | 3698.570 / 5649 s | 5315.78 / 3480.40 | 97.778 / 149.076 | PASS |

These points ran on different pairs and are reported only as standalone steady-state and accuracy evidence; no J2 before/after ratio is claimed. The formal speedup is the J1 same-allocation comparison above.

**Why `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE=1` is not a mitigation:** a queue owns one `transfer_worker`. That worker processes one room's destination sessions in sequence and waits for the room's submitted transfer futures before dequeuing another room. Threads parallelize per-layer work inside the current room; they do not make rooms on one queue concurrent. J1 shows the distinction directly: Q1 concentrates all 9 executor threads and improves the broken Q4 baseline by 26.1%, but its busy-worker count remains one and the room-sharded fix is another 46.8% faster. Q1 also removes useful queue parallelism from topologies whose old key happened to spread rooms, so it is not a topology-independent replacement for room sharding.

Native samples put all active executor threads below `batch_transfer_sync`, with top frames in mutex wait, `cuStreamQuery`, and `cuMemcpyBatchAsync_v2`. Increasing capacity from Q4/thread8 to Q8/thread16 reduced throughput by 7.1%, so the residual shared-engine contention is outside this patch.

The speedup scope is transfer-bound workloads such as Qwen3.8, whose transfer is about 442 MiB per request. For compute-bound models such as Qwen3.5 DEP, an external Q=1 comparison found queue distribution changes throughput by only about 1%; that result is context, not a benchmark produced by this PR.

CPU tests: `test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py` 13/13; the cross-queue fail-fast mutation is RED before restoring the shared-session check and GREEN afterward. `ruff format --check` and `git diff --check` pass; the file has no new Ruff diagnostics beyond three pre-existing findings.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body:
Independent GLM-5.2/ROCm evidence supporting the room hash here (our inventory S03/S11); we will track this PR instead of opening a duplicate.

With a DCP decode replica, every room had the same destination-session set, so destination-port hashing left one transfer worker active per prefill rank. Plain `room % 4` also failed: the room residue encoded the prefill DP rank. In our historical `dcpx6 -> dcpx7b` experiment, hashing the room changed sampled active workers from 1 to 2–4 per rank and measured KV-transfer p50 from 21.3 s to 11.3 s. `dcpx7` with plain modulo did not spread work. This agrees with the congruent-room case already covered by your tests.

There is also a caution: same-node `g4tune R1 (dest) -> R2 (mix)` reduced mean transfer time from 9.98 s to 2.16 s, but TPOT worsened from about 13.3 ms to 15 ms; we did not adopt that configuration. Both comparisons are single historical runs with simulated MTP acceptance. They are transfer diagnostics, not model-accuracy validation or a claim that stack throughput belongs to this patch. The later GLM stack's PP-overlap/custom-all-reduce correctness problems also prevent using its throughput as patch evidence.

Archived evidence: `glm52.v0521-g4tune-xfer.packup_20261020` and `glm52.dcpx-pack-fix-best.packup_20261023`. Our layer-group parallelism and instrumentation are separate experiments, not additional functionality requested for this PR.

@@ -82,6 +82,16 @@
     "Number of mooncake_session_ids un-blacklisted via probe.",
 )
 
+_UINT64_MASK = (1 << 64) - 1
+
+
+def _mix_room_id(room: int) -> int:
+    """Return the SplitMix64 hash of an integer room ID."""
+    mixed = (room + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) & _UINT64_MASK
+    mixed = ((mixed ^ (mixed >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) & _UINT64_MASK
+    mixed = ((mixed ^ (mixed >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB) & _UINT64_MASK
+    return (mixed ^ (mixed >> 31)) & _UINT64_MASK
+
 
 # decode
 @dataclasses.dataclass
@@ -2717,12 +2727,8 @@ def add_transfer_request(
             # add further chunks into the transfer queue.
             return
 
-        # NOTE(shangming): sharding according to the dst_infos to make sure
-        # requests with the same dst_sessions will be added into the same
-        # queue, which enables early abort with failed sessions.
-        dst_infos = self.transfer_infos[bootstrap_room].keys()
-        session_port_sum = sum(int(session.rsplit(":", 1)[1]) for session in dst_infos)
-        shard_idx = session_port_sum % len(self.transfer_queues)
+        # Room IDs can be congruent with their DP rank, so mix all bits first.
+        shard_idx = _mix_room_id(bootstrap_room) % len(self.transfer_queues)
 
         if trace_ctx is None:
             trace_ctx = TraceNullContext()

+            transfer_queues=queues,
+        )
+        manager.check_status = lambda room: manager.request_status[room]
+        return manager, queued_rooms
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _enqueue(manager, room):
+        MooncakeKVManager.add_transfer_request(
+            manager,
+            bootstrap_room=room,
+            kv_indices=np.array([room], dtype=np.int32),
+            index_slice=slice(None),
+            is_last_chunk=False,

issue_comments.body:
Independent GLM-5.2/ROCm evidence supporting the room hash here (our inventory S03/S11); we will track this PR instead of opening a duplicate.

With a DCP decode replica, every room had the same destination-session set, so destination-port hashing left one transfer worker active per prefill rank. Plain `room % 4` also failed: the room residue encoded the prefill DP rank. In our historical `dcpx6 -> dcpx7b` experiment, hashing the room changed sampled active workers from 1 to 2–4 per rank and measured KV-transfer p50 from 21.3 s to 11.3 s. `dcpx7` with plain modulo did not spread work. This agrees with the congruent-room case already covered by your tests.

There is also a caution: same-node `g4tune R1 (dest) -> R2 (mix)` reduced mean transfer time from 9.98 s to 2.16 s, but TPOT worsened from about 13.3 ms to 15 ms; we did not adopt that configuration. Both comparisons are single historical runs with simulated MTP acceptance. They are transfer diagnostics, not model-accuracy validation or a claim that stack throughput belongs to this patch. The later GLM stack's PP-overlap/custom-all-reduce correctness problems also prevent using its throughput as patch evidence.

Archived evidence: `glm52.v0521-g4tune-xfer.packup_20261020` and `glm52.dcpx-pack-fix-best.packup_20261023`. Our layer-group parallelism and instrumentation are separate experiments, not additional functionality requested for this PR.
